review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν.
5:1.targetText: On the other side of the sea, they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

5:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου, εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ,
5:2.targetText: As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, He was met by a man with an unclean spirit, who was coming from the tombs.

groups.note: The genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ ("he") is rendered with the name Jesus.
εὐθύς ("immediately"), which in Greek goes with the meeting, is rendered by the temporal "As soon as".
The active "met him" is made passive in English.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause; the Greek has only "from the tombs".

5:3.sourceText: ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν, καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι
5:3.targetText: This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained, even with chains.

groups.note: The relative pronoun ὅς ("who") begins a new English sentence as "This man".
τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ("had his dwelling") is rendered as one verb phrase.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes "no one could bind him" passive, so οὐδείς ("no one") has no separate English word.
BSB's passive leaves the object αὐτόν ("him") unexpressed.

5:4.sourceText: διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσιν δεδέσθαι, καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι·
5:4.targetText: Though he was often bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and shattered the shackles. Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him.

groups.note: διὰ τό with the infinitive ("because he had been bound") is recast as a concessive clause.
The passive "torn apart by him" (ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ) is made active, so the agent becomes the subject.
ἴσχυεν ("was strong enough") is rendered "with the strength".

unmappedSource.reason: The καί joining the infinitives is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an existential frame; the verb ἴσχυεν is rendered "with the strength".

5:5.sourceText: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.
5:5.targetText: Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.

groups.note: διὰ παντός ("continually") with the periphrastic ἦν κράζων ("was crying out") is rendered "he kept crying out".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB omits the initial Greek and at this verse boundary.

5:6.sourceText: καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν,
5:6.targetText: When the man saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees before Him.

groups.note: The participle ἰδών is rendered as a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the participle.

5:7.sourceText: καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου; ὁρκίζω σε τὸν Θεόν, μή με βασανίσῃς.
5:7.targetText: And he shouted in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!”

groups.note: Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ("what to me and to you?") is an idiom of protest.

unmappedSource.reason: The verb λέγει ("says") introducing the quotation is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies question support in the idiom; the Greek has no verb.
English supplies a verb for the idiom; the Greek has no verb.

5:8.sourceText: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
5:8.targetText: For Jesus had already declared, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγεν ("he was saying") is rendered as an earlier command.
The nominative with the article (τὸ πνεῦμα) is used as a vocative, so the address "you" goes with it.

unmappedSource.reason: The dative αὐτῷ ("to him") is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek has only the verb ending.

5:9.sourceText: καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν Τί ὄνομά σοι; καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι, ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν.
5:9.targetText: “What is your name?” Jesus asked.  “My name is Legion,” he replied, “for we are many.”

The pronouns αὐτόν ("him") and αὐτῷ ("to him") are not separately expressed.

English supplies the verb; the Greek question has none.

5:10.sourceText: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered with the name Jesus.
ἵνα with the subjunctive after "begged" is rendered as an English infinitive.

5:11.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη·

groups.note: πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ("near the hill") is rendered "on the nearby hillside".

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

5:12.sourceText: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν.
5:12.targetText: So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered with the name Jesus.
εἰσέλθωμεν with εἰς ("enter into") is rendered by the one verb "enter".

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") introducing the quotation is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

5:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς. καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ὡς δισχίλιοι, καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
5:13.targetText: He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle "came out" to the main verb; the Greek has no conjunction here.
English attaches the number to the herd; ὡς δισχίλιοι stands in apposition.

5:14.sourceText: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς· καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός.
5:14.targetText: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτούς ("them") is rendered "the pigs".
BSB's one "in the" serves both εἰς τὴν πόλιν and εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB condenses "what it is that had happened" (τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός), so ἐστιν has no separate word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for "reported"; the Greek has none.
English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

5:41.sourceText: καὶ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ παιδίου λέγει αὐτῇ Ταλιθὰ κούμ, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Τὸ κοράσιον, σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε.
5:41.targetText: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”

groups.note: τοῦ παιδίου ("of the child") is rendered by the pronoun her.
ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον ("is, when translated") is rendered "means".
The nominative with the article (τὸ κοράσιον) is used as a vocative.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The dative αὐτῇ ("to her") is not separately expressed.

5:42.sourceText: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέστη τὸ κοράσιον καὶ περιεπάτει· ἦν γὰρ ἐτῶν δώδεκα. καὶ ἐξέστησαν εὐθὺς ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ.
5:42.targetText: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around. She was twelve years old, and at once they were utterly astounded.

groups.note: The cognate phrase ἐκστάσει μεγάλῃ ("with great amazement") is rendered "utterly".

5:43.sourceText: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἵνα μηδεὶς γνοῖ τοῦτο, καὶ εἶπεν δοθῆναι αὐτῇ φαγεῖν.
5:43.targetText: Then Jesus gave strict orders that no one should know about this, and He told them to give her something to eat.

groups.note: BSB moves αὐτοῖς ("to them"), the people given the orders, to "He told them".
The passive δοθῆναι ("to be given") is rendered with the active "give".
